poseReferencePrompt: Edit only the anatomical RIGHT arm (screen LEFT) of this exact approved bust portrait to add a believable, very small greeting. This is a POSE REFERENCE to design an animation, not a new character. Preserve the face, blue bob hair, mole, identity, gaze, expression, head, neck, shoulders, white/blue suit and left arm. Keep the same front camera, portrait framing, soft lighting and transparent background. The right upper arm remains close beside the torso, the elbow naturally bends below the bottom of the bust framing, the right forearm inclines gently upward toward the screen-left side of the chest, and the right hand gives a reserved greeting next to the outer lapel. Fingertips must stay BELOW the chin and clear of the face and hair. The hand must be anatomically proportional to this body, connected convincingly through wrist, cuff, forearm, elbow and upper sleeve. Palm in a soft THREE-QUARTER angle toward camera rather than a flat frontal stop-sign. Four fingers stay relatively close with soft natural curvature and staggered fingertips; thumb relaxed, not stretched sideways. No rigid spread-finger pose, no pointing, no exaggerated waving, no detached hand, no doll arm, no plastic or translucent skin, no jewelry. The pose should feel like a real person's gentle 'hello' during conversation. Show sufficient cuff and sleeve for judging the full kinematic chain. Do not change the head or torso design to accommodate the arm. Highest priority: human anatomical credibility and understated body language in the context of the existing person.
cutoutPrompt: Extract ONLY the raised anatomical right forearm and hand on screen LEFT from this exact portrait into a clean transparent sprite. Keep the existing natural curled fingers, three-quarter palm, wrist, light-blue shirt cuff, and white suit sleeve with blue trim unchanged in design, lighting, proportions and pose. Include the entire raised sleeve down through its cut at the bottom image edge. Remove the head, hair, neck, torso, tie, lapels, and the upper arm/background behind the raised forearm. This is a cutout of the raised forearm, not a new upright hand design. Preserve the same 1122 by 1402 canvas and the SAME PIXEL PLACEMENT: fingertips near x230/y775, wrist near x290/y1160, sleeve continues diagonally down to the bottom left. Leave everything else fully transparent without halos. Do not recenter or enlarge the arm. No cast shadow outside its contour. Five relaxed anatomically credible fingers, not a flat spread-finger stop sign.
